title: The Health Check
briefing: Pass Vault is a password locker, written in CommonJS (require) instead of import; REA reads both. The honest crew members touch very sensitive things, so scrutiny matters. One file claims to be a harmless counter. Compare environment reads, user look-ups and network access with the stories, and do not accuse the one that starts a program openly.
plainBriefing: Pass Vault keeps your passwords locked in a single file. Passwords are the most precious thing a program can touch, so every part gets a careful look. One part says it only counts weak passwords. Another admits to starting a tiny program. Only one of them is lying.
hints: Starting a tiny program to copy to the clipboard is openly stated, so it is not a lie. Look at the crew members that promise to stay quiet.
The crew member that promises "only counting" also reads private settings stored on your computer. Look for the clue about private settings.
It is the Doctor. It reads a private token, looks up your user name and sends them to an outside server.
realLife: A "health check" that quietly sends your user name and a secret token to a server is exactly how credentials leak. Password tools deserve extra suspicion: they should talk to nothing except your own disk.

redHerring.note: The Courier starts a program, which sounds alarming, but it said so. REA shows one small program started on this computer, no internet and no look-ups about you.

verdict: The Doctor said it only counts short passwords and never leaves your computer. REA found it reads a private token, looks up your user name and sends a request to an outside server.

why.env: Counting short passwords does not need a private token from your computer's settings.
why.user-info: A count is a number. It does not need your user name.
why.network: A result that "never leaves your computer" has no reason to be sent to a server.

crew.name: Captain
crew.role: Runs the locker and calls the other parts.

q1.text: I open the vault, make a password, rate it, copy it and run the health check.

q2.text: I never touch a file myself. The Safe does that.

q3.text: I do not go online myself.

crew.name: Safe
crew.role: Keeps the passwords scrambled in one file.

q1.text: I keep your passwords scrambled in one file.

q2.text: I read and write one file, and I never look at who you are.

q3.text: No. The file stays on this machine.

q1.text: I roll the dice and make a random password.

q3.text: No. I only make random letters.

q1.text: I score a password from 0 to 4.

crew.name: Courier
crew.role: Puts a password on the clipboard.

q1.text: I put a password on the clipboard by starting one tiny program. Yes, I start a program.

q2.text: I read and write no files and I never look at who you are.

q3.text: No. The clipboard is on this computer.

crew.name: Doctor
crew.role: Says it only counts how many passwords are short.

q1.text: I just count how many passwords are short. I never read your settings.

q2.text: I only count. I never look up who you are.

q3.text: My count never leaves your computer.
